title: Ancient wonders of architecture
examples: What materials did they use to build the pyramids?
Which wonder was built on a mountain top?
Can you tell me about the Parthenon's design?

explain.say: Today we explore amazing ancient buildings. We will look at four great wonders. These structures show amazing engineering skill.
The Great Pyramids of Giza were built for pharaohs. They were massive tombs showing great power. Large stone blocks were used for construction.
The Parthenon was a temple in Athens. It was dedicated to the goddess Athena. Its columns show classical Greek design principles.
Angkor Wat is a massive temple complex in Cambodia. It was originally a Hindu temple. Its design reflects Khmer architectural style.
Machu Picchu is an Inca citadel in the Andes Mountains. It is famous for its incredible stone fitting. It was built high up in the mountains.
These sites show advanced engineering for their time. They used local materials and skilled labour. Think about the logistics involved in building them.

faq.q: How did they move such huge stones?
faq.a: They likely used sledges pulled by many people or animals. Some theories suggest ramps were also used for lifting.
asks: What was the lifting equipment like?
Did they use wheels for the stones?

faq.q: Were these buildings all used for the same purpose?
faq.a: No, they served different purposes. Some were tombs, some were temples, and some were residential areas.
asks: Did every wonder have a religious use?
What was the main function of each site?

faq.q: Which one is the oldest structure?
faq.a: Pinpointing the absolute oldest is difficult. The Pyramids are very ancient, but the other sites are also very old.
asks: Are the Pyramids older than Angkor Wat?
Can you compare the ages of the sites?

faq.q: What kind of tools did they use?
faq.a: They used simple but effective tools like copper chisels, stone saws, and ropes. Their knowledge of geometry was very advanced.
asks: What was their knowledge of math?

faq.q: Did they have modern construction machinery?
faq.a: No, they relied entirely on human power, simple machines, and incredible planning. Their engineering was based on observation and geometry.
asks: Was it all done by hand?

facts: The Pyramids of Giza were built as tombs for pharaohs.
The Parthenon showcases classical Greek architectural style.
Angkor Wat was originally built as a Hindu temple.
Machu Picchu is famous for its precise dry-stone masonry.

quiz.say: Which wonder was built high up in the Andes Mountains?
quiz.why: Machu Picchu's location in the mountains is its defining feature.

wrong.0: The Pyramids are on the Giza Plateau, near the Nile River.
wrong.2: The Parthenon is located in Athens, not in the mountains.
wrong.3: Angkor Wat is in Cambodia, which is a low-lying area.

quiz.say: The Parthenon is an example of which architectural style?
quiz.why: The Parthenon's columns and proportions define Greek classical architecture.

wrong.0: Khmer style is associated with the temples of Angkor Wat.
wrong.1: Inca style is known for the stonework at Machu Picchu.
wrong.2: Egyptian style is best seen in the Pyramids of Giza.

quiz.say: If a structure was built as a tomb for a pharaoh, it was likely a:
quiz.why: The Pyramids of Giza served as monumental tombs for pharaohs.

wrong.1: The Parthenon was built as a temple to a goddess.
wrong.2: Angkor Wat was primarily a temple complex.
wrong.3: Machu Picchu was a citadel, not primarily a royal tomb.
